newsitem.title: USA: World's oldest mom is victory for women - doctors.
newsitem.headline: World's oldest mom is victory for women - doctors.

text.p: Doctors who treated the oldest woman ever to give birth brushed aside the fact she lied about her age, saying on Thursday the 63-year-old first-time mother's achievement was a blow for sexual equality.

"I would argue that this has been going on for a long time with men; this just levels the playing field for women," said Dr. Richard Paulson, professor of obstetrics and gynecology at the University of Southern California.
"Human beings have been becoming parents in their 50's and 60's for a long time," Paulson told reporters, but added that until now, it was only men.

The professor also heads USC's Programme for Assisted Reproduction, which announced on Wednesday that a woman had given birth at the age of 63 years and nine months as a result of in-vitro fertilisation.
Paulson said the woman, who asked to remain anonymous, was the oldest on record to give birth. A woman in Italy had a baby last year at the age of 62.

"It might be said that women have not one, but two biological clocks. The clock with the eggs and ovaries seems to run out much earlier than the one for the uterus and the remainder of the reproductive system," he said.

The university said in a statement that the woman, who had been trying to get pregnant since she married 16 years earlier, had a baby girl by Caesarian section, at an undisclosed hospital last last year and that she and her daughter are in good health. She was breast-feeding, Paulson said.
At a news conference at the Loma Linda Medical Centre, some 60 miles (90 km) east of Los Angeles, Dr. Hermina Salvador said she had delivered the baby there on Nov. 7.

"Before I saw her, one of the girls at the front desk said 'You're seeing a 63-year-old patient.' I thought she was kidding me. I still did not believe it until I saw the patient," Salvador told reporters.
She said the patient, who she referred to as "a religious lady," developed diabetes about halfway through her pregnancy and had to watch her diet.
Apart from that there were no other complications, although the doctor monitored the woman's condition every week, instead of every four weeks as in a younger patient.
"The success story depends on the patient and without her cooperation, willingness and compliance I don't think we would have had the happy ending," Salvador said.

Through the in-vitro method, a donated egg was fertilised with sperm from the woman's 60-year-old husband and the embryo implanted in her. The first attempt was unsuccessful, but the second fertilised egg was accepted by the woman's body and developed naturally, Paulson said.
"The first time we saw the heartbeat in the baby, she (the mother) held my hand and tears came in my eyes," said Dr. Melvin Thornton, who treated the woman.

USC doctors said the woman lied about her age in order to enter the infertility programme, which has a maximum age limit of 55. She apparently produced documents from another hospital giving her age at the time she started the treatment as 50, when in fact she was 60.
"Our consciousness has been raised to the issue of people deceiving us about their age," said Paulson, who stressed the woman passed a rigorous cardio-vascular physical examination.
However, officials said that in the future they would carry out more stringent background checks on patients, although there were no plans to change the 55-year age limit.
Paulson compared giving birth at an advanced age to such things as climbing Mt. Everest. "I'd say, 'Gosh, good for them,'" he said.
